chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Wahb ibn Wahb has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu Al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb Al-Qadi Al-Qurashi.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْقَاضِي: The Judge, a title indicating judicial authority
key_terms.الْقُرَشِيُّ: Al-Qurashi, indicating lineage from the Quraysh tribe
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both, a honorific for two individuals
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sad ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.وَهْبِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ: Wahb ibn Wahb, a specific narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Wahb ibn Wahb in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s personal attestation (tadhkirah) of the chain, emphasizing the reliability of his direct transmission from his father, a key figure in the Saduq family's scholarly lineage. It underscores the importance of the 'Thiqah' (reliable) narrators in Shia hadith sciences, particularly linking the early Kufi jurist Wahb ibn Wahb to the later Imami tradition through prominent intermediaries like Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan al-Saffar.
